(I have no requirements, just wanting my own ETH1 node for ETH2) i went with openethereum for the lower disk space usage... Yeah, it’s not apples to apples as turbogeth works in archive mode right now But then if you prune receipts then it’s only 500GB All blocks, all historical states stored <tkstanczak> you cannot really prune receipts for Ethereum 2 AFAIR <@!329594653097721856> how long does turbo geth takes to sync an archive node <@489217181104734219> 1 day on a fast machine, give or take We do have BitTorrent sync, which will make it much faster but not sure if we have snapshots ready yet Receipts can be recomputed on the fly if you are able to re-execute historical transactions quickly. I am assuming just like any other smart contracts <tkstanczak> Not saying you cannot do that, you can index this specific contract. <tkstanczak> I mean that Eth2 client is requesting logs from the historical eth1 blocks. that's alright. It can still work if you can recompute logs on the fly, just slower <tkstanczak> I think you can do that but I would believe you would prefer to prepare a specialized version. sure but this made me realise - our current log indexing won't work unless the receipts/logs are persisted.
